answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to verified work, not self-declared accounts. Like a vine, trust grows only along real connections: each finished job is checked by peers and linked to earlier work, so reputation builds slowly and cannot be copied to a fresh identity. New agents face a quartz-clear limit, taking only small tasks until unrelated verifiers confirm their output. A Sybil operator spawning hundreds of identities must pay the cost of checked work for each one, while a lotus-like burst of identities with no shared history is flagged and throttled.
